$comment: The platform-suite registry (engineering/development.md § Platform suites). One entry per check that must run on a real macOS or Windows runner. `os`: runner labels (macos-latest, windows-latest). `paths`: globs; a PR that touches one runs the suite, and the nightly and a manual dispatch run every suite. `run`: the command, from the repo root after `npm ci` and `npm run build`. `why`: what this suite proves that Linux cannot. tools/check-ownership.js (checkPlatformSuites) fails on a malformed entry or a `run` that names a file that is gone.

suites.name: export-confine
suites.why: A render reads a local file only by REAL path inside the deck folder (media note §4.11). macOS reaches /tmp and $TMPDIR through symlinks (/private/tmp, /private/var), the case a real-path check gets wrong first; Linux cannot show it. The Mermaid worker's own page applies the same check. Windows is not listed: the CLI now builds its file URLs with pathToFileURL, but a Windows runner cannot reach the suite, because `npm run build` aborts at tools/check-ownership.js (its gates compare backslash paths against forward-slash allowlists; run 39197530212, job 117883739719), so the CLI's dist/ bundles are not built there. Re-add windows-latest once that gate is Windows-clean (followups.d/2786-p2-check-ownership-on-windows.md); until then the Windows file-URL change is UNVERIFIED on a Windows run.

suites.name: wait-for-macos
suites.run: for t in timeout gtimeout flock perl; do command -v $t || echo "no $t"; done; brew install coreutils && node --test test/unit/tools/wait-for.test.js test/unit/tools/warn-unbounded-wait.test.js
suites.why: tools/wait-for.sh takes its lock with flock(1) or, where that is missing, perl's flock builtin, and needs GNU timeout (gtimeout on macOS). macOS ships neither flock(1) nor timeout, so the perl path and the exit-69 'missing dependency' path are the ones a Mac takes; Linux tests drive them only by pinning WAIT_FOR_LOCK_IMPL and a controlled PATH (engineering/development.md § Waiting for a slow job: 'macOS itself remains UNVERIFIED'). The first two runs (jobs 117883739691, 117885882571) showed a stock macOS runner has perl but no timeout, gtimeout or flock; the tests failed because their lock probe called flock(1), not because wait-for.sh did (its own run-mode test passed). The probe now falls back to perl, and the entry installs coreutils first (the supported state).
